title: A different writer restating a fact does not reorder it
what: The poisoning guard of the restated-note rule (A33). Alice records a fact; later Bob, another writer, writes a note that gives the same fact key another value. Monomem must not put Bob's note in front of Alice's on his say-so (an attacker could bury a true note that way): the order stays as the search ranks it, nothing is labelled as restated, and Alice's note carries the dispute marker instead.
